description: Replace unapproved words (utilize, terminate, commence, prior to) with STE-approved words.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses only STE-approved verbs?
options: Utilize the wrench to loosen the bolt.
Use the wrench to loosen the bolt.
Commence loosening the bolt with the wrench.
questions.explanation: 'Utilize' and 'commence' are not in the STE dictionary. Use 'use' and 'start'.

questions.prompt: Tap the words that are not STE-approved:
questions.sentence: Prior to the test, examine the oil level.
questions.explanation: 'Prior to' is not approved in STE. Always use 'before'.

questions.prompt: Which word is the STE-approved replacement for 'commence'?
questions.explanation: The STE dictionary gives 'start' for this meaning. 'Commence' and 'initiate' are not approved.

questions.prompt: Tap the word that is not STE-approved:
questions.sentence: Terminate the pump if the pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: 'Terminate' is not approved in STE. Use 'stop'.

questions.prompt: Write this step in STE: 'Utilize a torque wrench to tighten the nut.'
questions.explanation: 'Utilize' and 'employ' are not approved in STE. Use the simple verb 'use'.

questions.prompt: Tap the word that is not STE-approved:
questions.sentence: Ensure that the valve is closed before you continue.
questions.explanation: 'Ensure' is not approved in STE. Use 'make sure'.

questions.prompt: Edit this step so it has 20 words or fewer. Keep 'before' and 'gloves':
questions.initialText: Prior to the commencement of the maintenance procedure, it is necessary that you utilize the approved safety gloves in order to prevent injury to your hands from the sharp edges.
questions.explanation: STE procedural sentences have a maximum of 20 words. 'Prior to' becomes 'before', 'utilize' becomes 'use' or 'put on', and 'in order to' becomes 'to'.
